submitted.rationale: Index 16 (Ba0.43Mn0.57) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 3.64e-6 A. The photoactive phase is probably BaMnO3: its MEGNet HSE gap is 2.73 eV, which absorbs 3.22 eV light, and XRD at indices 5 and 20 matches a BaMnO3-like pattern. Ba-rich index 20 dropped to 4e-8 A. Index 5 (Ba 0.49) gave 2.95e-6 A.

rejected.reason: Measured 4e-8 A; the Ba-rich side is much worse.
Predicted gaps of the Mn-rich phases BaMn4O8 (0.89 eV) and Ba2Mn3O8 (0.34 eV) are narrow, so poor photoanode behavior is likely.

consultations.verdict: Support: MEGNet HSE gap of 2H-BaMnO3 is 2.73 eV (absorbs the 3.22 eV light, and the gap is wide enough for the voltage a photoanode needs). Mn-rich BaMn4O8 (0.89 eV) and Ba2MnO4 (1.11 eV) have narrow gaps and are likely poor. XRD at index 5 shows a BaMnO3-like pattern.

Mixed but supportive. Ba4Mn3O10 (1.42 eV) has a narrower gap, but Ba3Mn2O8 at Ba 0.6 has a 3.07 eV gap (from earlier), just below the 3.22 eV photons. Index 20 shows an extra 2.20 peak beyond BaMnO3, and it is a GP top-5 pick, so probing the Ba-rich side is worthwhile.

Against going far Mn-rich: Ba2Mn3O8 at Ba 0.4 has a 0.34 eV gap, so the photoactive phase is likely BaMnO3 (2.73 eV). Index 16 (Ba 0.43) is still near BaMnO3, a bit Mn-richer (the Ba-rich side dropped sharply), and has the highest GP mean. That favors 16 over 12.
